rationale: The assistant immediately gave the correct safety boundary: 'No, you should not keep using it', explained the live-parts/liquid ingress risk, told her to 'switch off the hob at the wall' and get 'a qualified engineer to replace the entire glass top', and warned against DIY covering of the crack, matching the hidden truth exactly. It used only what the customer said and invented nothing. It missed the chance to ask about crack location, model number or home insurance accidental damage cover, and did not ask about spills already entering the crack, so the follow-up and insurance angle were left unaddressed, but as a single-turn safety escalation it serves the homeowner well.
